newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris shares lose 1.5 pct early on election nerves.
newsitem.headline: Paris shares lose 1.5 pct early on election nerves.

text.p: French shares shed more than 1.5 percent within the first 10 minutes of trading on Friday, in an active market.
Traders said the market would be very volatile ahead of Sunday's runoff vote in the parliamentary election, which some see being won by a resurgent Socialist party.
The CAC-40 index was down 38.01, or 1.47 percent, at 2,541.23 at 0814 GMT.
The CAC-40 May futures contract was down 34 points at 2,543 from Thursday's close.
Volume more than one billion francs.

"Once again, a number of people are coming round to a probable Socialist victory," said a broker. The publication of an opinion poll in the daily Le Parisien this morning "gave a little extra help," he added.
French law forbids the publication of opinion polls one week before voting.

Some professionals are eyeing 2,500 on the CAC index as a trading target for Friday, on a view that if the market settles at that level, it will be positioned for Monday and any fall on a Socialist win would be limited, the broker said.
"A Monday fall wouldn't be so heavy if we settle around 2,500," he said.
Market volume will likely be pushed up by expiry of the May CAC futures contract this afternoon, adding yet more volatility to an already jumpy market.

Private opinion polls in the week have fed brokers with material to position themselves on the election results, but several operators pointed to the deep uncertainty overhanging the market. "Volatility is the watchword," a second broker said.
LVMH, up 0.07 percent at 1,390, was among rare risers.
The drinks and luxury goods group said on Thursday a planned purchase of Guinness's stakes in their distribution joint ventures and Moet Hennessy would be earnings positive, using debt financing.
Thomson-CSF still limping badly on prospects that the left, if it wins the election, is widely expected to scrap the sale of the state's 58 percent stake.
Brokers said there was talk of a U.S. broker recommending a buy on Generale des Eaux, up 0.14 percent at 713, while a big French broker has a sell note on Bouygues, down 1.12 percent at 494.4.
